source.text: Do not report physicalism as refuted merely because the reconstructed text records an explanatory gap.
source.locator: Printed pp. 439-442, especially notes 6 and 8; p. 446 on the conclusion about physicalism

reading.speaker: Thomas Nagel
reading.summary: Do not report physicalism as refuted merely because the reconstructed text records an explanatory gap.

review.rationale: Imported design requirement; requires source-fidelity review. Mutation control: Strengthening a qualified explanatory conclusion into an unrestricted impossibility or falsity claim must be identified as a changed argument.

premises: Preserve the experiencer and the perspective from which a description is understood.
Distinguish first-person understanding from externally available physical description.
Preserve qualifications concerning current explanatory understanding.
Distinguish an epistemic or explanatory difficulty from the falsity of an ontological thesis.
claim.conclusion: No numerical or Boolean assignment alone adjudicates the phenomenological claim; unsupported semantics remain review-required.
